response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT link_to_budget, SUM(cost) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n FROM expense WHERE link_to_budget IS NOT NULL GROUP BY link_to_budget), a AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS av FROM t) SELECT AVG(t.total) AS avg_total, SUM(t.n) AS total_expenses, AVG(t.total - a.av) AS avg_excess FROM t, a WHERE t.total > a.av

assumptions.assumption: Budget lines are those that have at least one expense. The average spend per budget line is the average of the per-budget SUM(cost) over those lines. Budget lines with no expenses are not counted as zero, and expenses with a NULL link_to_budget are ignored.
The expense count is the number of expense rows belonging to the above-average budget lines. The average excess is the mean of (line total minus the overall average).

alternatives.interpretation: The average spend per budget line also counts budget lines with no expenses as 0. The average is taken over all rows in the budget table.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT b.budget_id, COALESCE(SUM(e.cost),0) AS total, COUNT(e.expense_id) AS n FROM budget b LEFT JOIN expense e ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id GROUP BY b.budget_id), a AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS av FROM t) SELECT AVG(t.total) AS avg_total, SUM(t.n) AS total_expenses, AVG(t.total - a.av) AS avg_excess FROM t, a WHERE t.total > a.av
